system.name: tnic
system.one_liner: a trusted NIC architecture providing a minimal, formally verified silicon root-of-trust for building trustworthy distributed systems

components.name: Host CPU
components.role: issues RDMA requests to the RoCE protocol kernel

components.name: Host memory
components.role: source/destination of DMA transfers for message payloads

components.name: PCIe DMA/Bridge IP
components.role: transfers data between host memory and the FPGA NIC

components.name: Attestation kernel
components.role: generates (Attest) and verifies (Verify) message attestations for non-equivocation and transferable authentication

components.name: Keystore
components.role: stores the shared secret keys used by HMAC

components.name: HMAC
components.role: generates message authentication codes (MAC) for attestation

components.name: Counters store
components.role: keeps per-session send/receive counters (send_cnts, recv_cnts) for non-equivocation

components.name: RoCE protocol kernel
components.role: implements the reliable IB/RDMA transport and network layers (RoCE v2)

components.name: Req handler
components.role: receives the request opcode issued by the host and initiates DMA fetch of payload

components.name: Request generation
components.role: constructs the outgoing network packet from the opcode and attested message, appending IB/UDP/IP headers

components.name: State tables
components.role: stores protocol queues and metadata (PSNs, MSNs, retransmission timer)

components.name: Cmd merger
components.role: merges command/data streams within the RoCE protocol kernel data path

components.name: Request decoder
components.role: extracts headers, metadata, and the attested message from received packets

components.name: ARP server
components.role: lookup table of MAC/IP address correspondences, used to resolve the remote MAC before transmission

components.name: 100Gb MAC
components.role: link layer connecting tnic to the network fabric over 100G Ethernet, with Tx/Rx interfaces

content.key_idea: tnic's hardware places an Attestation kernel (Keystore, HMAC, Counters store) inline in the RoCE protocol kernel's data pipeline between PCIe DMA and the network, attesting every outgoing message and verifying every incoming one.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Host CPU/memory feed PCIe DMA into the Attestation kernel, which sits between the RoCE protocol kernel's transmit and receive paths, out through the ARP server/100Gb MAC to the network.

summary: tnic is a trusted NIC architecture that embeds a formally verified root-of-trust in a SmartNIC's hardware. This figure details that hardware: inside the Trusted FPGA NIC, a PCIe DMA/Bridge IP connects to Host CPU and Host memory, and an Attestation kernel sits inline between the DMA and the RoCE protocol kernel. The Attestation kernel's Keystore holds per-session shared keys, its HMAC module computes message authentication codes, and its Counters store tracks monotonic send/receive counters for non-equivocation. The RoCE protocol kernel implements the reliable IB/RDMA transport: a Req handler and Request generation module build outgoing packets (appending IB, UDP/IP headers) using an ARP server for MAC lookup and a 100Gb MAC for the link layer, while a Request decoder parses incoming packets and routes them back through the Attestation kernel for verification before delivery to host memory. Blue axes trace the transmission path and red axes trace the reception path.
